### ① Derived judgments

1. Crash fixed at every title render in `DashboardPreview.tsx`: RIGHT. Every site in the head file that turns `widget.title` / `w.title` into a React child or a string: line 73 `label: resolveInlineI18nLabel(w?.title, locale) || widgetId` (selection label, string, unchanged from base); line 93 to 97 `handleAddWidget` seeds `title` as a plain string and passes that string as the label; line 117 the rename write (a value, never rendered); line 122 `label: trimmed || id` (string); line 232 `const currentTitle = resolveInlineI18nLabel(widget.title, locale) ?? widget.id ?? ''` and line 302 `{currentTitle || ‹untitled›}`. Base line was `(widget.title as string | undefined) ?? widget.id ?? ''`, which handed the map to line 302 as a child. The spec resolver returns a `string` or `undefined` for any input (`i18n-label-resolver.ts`: string pass-through, non-object → `undefined`, map → six limbs → `undefined` on miss), so no object can reach line 302 or the input's `value` (line 271, seeded from `currentTitle` at 234 and re-synced at 238 to 241). The hint at line 158 uses only `widgets.length`. The grid cards are rendered by `DashboardRenderer` outside this file with `pickLocalized`, which also never yields an object. Nothing in the preview prints `[object Object]` for a map title.

2. Same resolver and locale: RIGHT. The strip uses `resolveInlineI18nLabel`, the alias of `@objectstack/spec/ui`'s `resolveI18nLabel` imported at line 28 of the same file since objectui#10835, the same function the selection label at line 73 already used; no new resolver import. The locale is the `locale` prop destructured at line 43, used at line 73 and handed to the strip at line 167. The host supplies it from `useMetadataLocale()` (`ResourceEditPage.tsx:430` → 2674), the same source `DashboardWidgetInspector` reads for its title (`MetadataInspectorProps.locale`). The grid cards in `DashboardRenderer` resolve with `pickLocalized(title, useObjectTranslation().language)`, the raw UI language; the parity test pins the two resolvers limb for limb, so they agree whenever the designer locale and the UI language agree, and the PR body records the `ja`-style divergence honestly as pre-existing.

3. The write: RIGHT, with the deviation disclosed. `setLocalized(value, language, next)` at head (`pickLocalized.ts:142` to 150): a non-object (string, `null`, `undefined`, array) returns `next`; a map returns `{ ...o, [localeWriteKey(o, language)]: next }`. `localeWriteKey` (lines 93 to 104): the exact tag if it holds a string, else the base language, else the first region sibling sharing the base, else the locale tag itself; own properties only, string values only. So the map is never flattened and every other entry survives, and the key written is the entry the resolver's limbs 1 to 3 display for that locale, so the strip re-renders exactly what was typed (round trip: exact → limb 1; base → limb 2; first regional sibling in insertion order → limb 3, same `Object.keys` order; the locale itself → limb 1). It differs from the literal `{ ...map, [locale]: draft }` only when the map lacks the exact tag but holds the base or a sibling, e.g. `{ en: 'Revenue' }` edited in `en-US`: `setLocalized` overwrites `en` (what the author saw), the literal spelling would add `en-US` and leave the displayed `en` string stale for `en` viewers. For the card's own case (`{ 'en-US', 'zh-CN' }` in `zh-CN`) and for the missing-locale case (`{ 'en-US' }` in `zh-CN` → adds `zh-CN`) the two spellings are identical, and both are pinned. This honours the ruling's intent (edit what you saw, never flatten, keep every other locale). It is the inspector's write for the same field: `DashboardWidgetInspector.tsx:290` `title: setLocalized(widget.title, locale, e.target.value) as DashboardWidgetSchema['title']`, with the read at 281 `resolveInlineI18nLabel(widget.title, locale)`, so the strip and the inspector now write the same entry under one rule. The PR body states the deviation and where it differs.

4. String title and the unchanged draft edges: RIGHT. `setLocalized('Revenue', locale, 'Sales')` is `'Sales'` (non-object branch), pinned by the control test. `commit` in the strip is byte-identical to base: `const v = draft.trim(); if (v && v !== currentTitle) onRename(v);` so an empty or whitespace draft writes nothing and a draft equal to the current title writes nothing, exactly as on base. For a string title `currentTitle` is the same string on both (resolver pass-through, `''` included); for an absent title both give `widget.id` (resolver returns `undefined` for `null`/`undefined`, then `?? widget.id`); so the "equal to current" comparison is the same comparison as before. `handleRenameWidget` still trims and still sets the selection label to `trimmed || id`.

5. Pins: RIGHT. `DashboardPreview.i18nTitle-10847.test.tsx` renders the real `DashboardPreview` (relative import) and the real `DashboardRenderer` (module-scope `import '@object-ui/plugin-dashboard'`, the AGENTS.md lazy-boundary discipline; the alias map resolves it to source), a host holding `draft` and `selection` in state, and selects by clicking `dashboard-preview-widget-rev` (the renderer's `data-testid` at `DashboardRenderer.tsx:953`). Red on base by mechanism: on base the strip throws for a map title, `PreviewErrorBoundary` swallows the tree, so `waitFor(() => screen.getByTitle('点击重命名'))` cannot resolve in tests 1, 2 and 3 (map titles), while test 4 (string title, `en-US`, `Click to rename`) passes on base, so 3 red / 1 green on base is what the file's mechanism yields and matches the dev's report. Ablation (the write replaced by `title: trimmed`): test 2 expects `{ 'en-US': 'Revenue', 'zh-CN': '营收' }` and would receive `'营收'`; test 3 expects `{ 'en-US': 'Revenue', 'zh-CN': '收入' }` and would receive `'收入'`; test 1 never renames and test 4 expects a string, so exactly 2 red / 2 green, consistent with the claim. Controls present: test 4 is the plain-string control, and test 1 asserts `queryByText('Preview failed to render')` is null. No timeout raised: the file sets no `testTimeout`, no per-test timeout, and is not in `vitest.config.mts`'s `heavyDomTests`. Test-hygiene note: the `vi.mock('@object-ui/react', …useAdapter)` is live, because `AdapterProvider.tsx:21` re-exports `useAdapter` from `@object-ui/react`, and it is the same pattern as the sibling `DashboardPreview.loneWidget.test.tsx`. Local run at head through the verify lock, once: queued 22:42:52Z, acquired after 174s, `RUN v4.1.10` in the throwaway worktree at `c527690`, `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 4 passed (4)`, start 22:45:48, duration 9.94s, `os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0 · held the lock 12s`. Green at head confirmed by me; red on base and the ablation are judged by mechanism above (no second run), and CI's eight `Test (shard …/8)` runs at the head, which include this file, all completed with success (poll 2).

6. Prose and shape: WRONG on one sentence. Shape is right: frontmatter is exactly `'@object-ui/app-shell': patch`, no `major`, app-shell is in the fixed group, `check-changeset-*` are green in CI; the PR body's first line is `Fixes #10847`; `Clause-②: no` holds, since the diff changes no export, no declared key and no accept set (`SelectedWidgetStrip` is module-private, `DashboardPreview`'s props are unchanged, the only new import is an existing `@object-ui/i18n` export). Sentences checked true against the head: the title is the spec's `I18nLabel` (`dashboard.zod.ts:812`); the strip rendered the stored value as a React child (base line 302); the error text and the "Preview failed to render" fallback (`PreviewShell.tsx:124`); the resolver is the spec's `resolveI18nLabel` in the designer locale and is the selection label's call (line 73); the draft is seeded from the same string (line 234); the save goes through `setLocalized`, the inspector's write (inspector line 290); a map title gets only its designer-locale entry replaced or added and every other locale kept (true in substance; the entry is the one the designer locale resolves to, see item 3); a plain-string title stays a plain string. The last sentence, "The inspector is still where every locale is edited.", is false at the head. The inspector's title field is a single-locale editor: it reads `resolveInlineI18nLabel(widget.title, locale)` and writes `setLocalized(widget.title, locale, …)` with `locale: SupportedLocale` (`'en-US' | 'zh-CN'`), exactly the pair the strip now uses, and its own comment at lines 273 to 277 says "Authoring EVERY locale from one panel is a different, still-open product question". No component under `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin` edits a locale map entry by entry (grep for `LocaleMap`, `LocalizedText`, `I18nLabelEditor`, `MultiLocale`, "every locale", "all locales", "each locale": only comments). A `ja` entry is reachable from neither surface. The sentence ships to consumers as `CHANGELOG.md` and tells them the inspector can do something it cannot. The same claim is repeated in the `SelectedWidgetStrip` docblock (`DashboardPreview.tsx:219`) and in the PR body. It echoes the triage's wording, but the triage is not evidence about the inspector's capability, and the dev cited the inspector's read/write pair while its comment says the opposite. Remedy: replace the sentence with a true one, e.g. "The inspector's title field edits the same entry through the same pair; authoring every locale from one surface remains open."

### ② Semver level

`patch` for `@object-ui/app-shell` is correct: a bug fix in a released package (AGENTS.md §9 Housekeeping and the objectstack post-task rule), no widening or narrowing of any declared key, export or accept set, so `Clause-②: no` and no `minor`; no `major`, per the version-alignment rule for the fixed group.

- Not a defect, recorded: the strip, the selection label and the inspector resolve in the designer locale (`useMetadataLocale`, two values), while `DashboardRenderer`'s cards resolve in the raw UI language; a UI language outside en/zh with a matching map entry shows one string on the card and another in the chrome, and the rename edits the chrome's entry. Pre-existing, disclosed in the PR body, no carrier.
